bark.speaker: FELDWEBEL
lines: Los, komm schon! Papiere her!
Na los, du da! Papiere — sofort!

choices.text: (Eyes on your shoes. A deaf man waits for a touch, not a voice.)
(Look up and hand the papers over.)

lines: (A pencil taps the table twice, in the corner of your eye. That, Jean can see. You hand the papers across.)
(Two taps of a pencil against the wood, at the edge of sight. Now you move. The papers cross the table.)
(You looked up at a voice. Deaf men look up at shadows and taps — never at voices. The Feldwebel's pen pauses over the page.)
(A voice moved you. Somewhere it is being written down that the deaf cousin answers German.)
(Eager, at a German bark. The wrong instinct, at the wrong speed. The pen pauses.)
(You obeyed a sound. The man by the pillar does not move, which is its own kind of note-taking.)
(Behind you a rifle-butt — or a case — cracks flat on the stones, loud as a shot.)
(Something heavy hits the cobbles behind you with a crack that makes the whole queue jump.)

choices.text: (Nothing. The street is silent to Jean. Let your eyes drift with the pigeons.)

lines: (Nothing. A pigeon lifts; your eyes follow it, mildly. The Feldwebel glances past you at whoever dropped it, annoyed.)
(The queue flinches as one animal — except you. You are watching a pigeon. The Feldwebel's annoyance goes over your head to the clumsy soldier behind.)
(A small flinch. Anyone would — anyone with ears.)
(Your shoulders answered the sound before you could stop them. Shoulders have ears.)
(You turned. Toward a sound. The pen writes something short.)
(A full turn, toward a noise that does not exist for Jean. Short of a signed confession, it is the loudest thing you own.)

exam.speaker: FELDWEBEL
lines: Jean Caillet. Sourd-muet, hm. — Ihre Mutter ist gestorben.
Caillet, Jean. Taubstumm, so so. — Deine Mutter ist tot, weißt du das?

choices.text: (The words are wind. Watch his pencil, bored, the way a man watches weather.)
(Hold still — but your jaw sets, one notch.)

lines: (Your mother is dead, he says, to a face that goes on being bored. The pencil taps, disappointed.)
(The oldest trap on the list, and it breaks on a bored face. He looks almost cheated.)
(Still — almost. A jaw is a small muscle with a loud voice. By the pillar, the long coat shifts its weight.)
(Your face held. Your jaw voted alone. The man by the pillar noticed the election.)
(One glance, to the far side of the barrier. Deaf men have nobody to check with. The pencil writes again.)
(You looked for her. One look. Jean Caillet, who has no one, looked for someone.)

stamp_q.speaker: FELDWEBEL
lines: Moment. Da fehlt ein Stempel. Wo ist der Stempel von der Präfektur, hm? Wo?
Halt — hier. Der Präfektur-Stempel fehlt. Wo ist der, hm? Antworte!

choices.text: (A missing stamp means nothing to a man who cannot hear the question. Wait, bored.)

lines: (He waves the card at your face. You look at it the way a horse looks at a newspaper. He mutters, finds the stamp on the other page himself.)
(The question hangs there, in a language you officially cannot lose. He finds the stamp himself and hates the page for it.)
(You pointed. At the answer. To a question asked in German. The forecourt goes very quiet around your finger.)
(One helpful finger, answering German it cannot hear. The pencil stops writing, which is worse than writing.)

fail.speaker: FELDWEBEL
lines: Der kommt mit. — HALT! Festhalten!
Den nehmen wir mit. HALT!
(The stamp comes down twice, bored as everything else here. The barrier lifts its arm like a tired man.)
(Two thumps of the stamp. The barrier swings up with a creak that means nothing at all — and everything.)
